resolution.note: Root cause: syncLockfile ran npm install --package-lock-only once with no retry against the registry and shared npm cache; one transient failure left no package-lock.json (init warning on stderr, s-lockfile-committed red), only under load. Could not reproduce in 80 concurrent runs (loop .krn/tmp/loop.sh: 5x4, 4x12, 5x4 of the ts test, all exit 0). Hardened: 3 attempts and --prefer-offline; regression tests at syncLockfile with a failing-then-passing npm; 20 of 20 under 4-way concurrency exit 0 after.

title: init ts standards test passes under parallel load
body:
Source: lead 2026-11-16: test/adopt/init.test.ts "--init ts … leaves zero failing standards" failed once in a lane's `npm run fast` under load and passed alone (handoff priority 1d).
Outcome: the root cause is named in the close note (which standard failed and why load changes it), and the test passes 20 of 20 runs of `node --test test/adopt/init.test.ts` while 4 parallel copies run (exit 0 each).
Why: a flaky gate costs every lane fast reruns, as the node_modules/.bin PATH leak did before #1151.
Proof: a loop script runs the test 20 times with 4 concurrent copies; all exit 0; a regression test pins the root cause at the lowest layer (KRN-14).
Files: test/adopt/init.test.ts, src/adopt/
